title: Retro game reconstruction discovery
summary: Review 29 game reconstructions, ports and game-specific editors.
notes: Personally compared project and source URLs against the current catalogue and checked pinned primary documentation and repository trees. No independent builds, gameplay or binary comparison.

sources.reason: The project extracts assets from an owned Amiga disk using an emulator at build time, then implements the game on Atari Lynx; the emulator is an extraction tool, not the Lynx runtime.
Ghidra-based reverse engineering and C11/SDL2 port of the 1995 DOS game.
Ghidra-based reverse engineering and C11/SDL2 port of the DOS episodes.
Ghidra-based reverse engineering and native source port of the DOS game.
Native Go recreation of five DOS winter-sport events. The project names it Sky or Die.
Native Go reconstruction of the 1991 DOS platform game.
Native Go reconstruction of the 1992 DOS naval game using recovered Pascal procedures and game resources.
Native macOS and Windows reimplementation using recovered DOS artwork, question data and sound streams.
New engine reads an owned copy of the DOS game's data and recreates its rules, maps and combat.
Native C++ reconstruction from the Lost Engines reverse-engineering project.
Native C++ reimplementation of the 1994 DOS game, from the Lost Engines project.
Structured 16-bit x86 assembly disassembly and source reconstruction for the DOS version.
Source-based 32X port of the DOS racing game, with shareware circuits and converted assets.
Work-in-progress SGDK port with converted original stage maps, graphics, collision and event data.
32X port built from the released public-domain source and the original retail resources.
32X port of the WinWar reimplementation, using user-supplied demo data.
SGDK 68000 port of the shareware episode, converting the original data at build time.
Master System port of the REminiscence engine's object-script interpreter using original game data.
AI-assisted decompilation covering The Black Gate and Serpent Isle, with a portable-source effort. The author reports byte-exact compiler checks.
Native Windows recreation of the 1989 game with documented research and a public beta.
Standalone browser editor for Raptor levels and enemy paths, based on documented recovered formats.
TypeScript tools and viewer for DOS game archives, assets, scripts, maps and save files.
Java castle editor with a separate work-in-progress native Atari ST edition.
Browser level editor for the DOS game's tiles, objects, triggers and other level features.
Browser editor with independently analysed file formats and decoded graphics.
Windows level editor reads original level banks and can patch the game executable.
Browser level editor based on reverse-engineered binary level formats.
Browser level editor built on the cyx reimplementation and independent DOS executable disassembly.
Browser level editor based on reverse-engineered formats and disassembled game logic.
